knowledge_point.title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{y^{2} - 1}{y^{2}}.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y\ne0$.

We need

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} - 1}{c^{2}}=0.
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=1$ and $y=-1$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y - \sin{\left(y \right)} - \pi.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

We need

$$
f(c) = - c - \sin{\left(c \right)} - \pi=0.
$$

- For $c=0$: Use $\sin{\left(0 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=- \pi + 0 - \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=- \pi$: Use $\sin{\left(- \pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(- \pi) &=- \pi - \sin{\left(- \pi \right)} + \pi \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=\pi$: Use $\sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\pi) &=- \pi - \pi - \sin{\left(\pi \right)} \\ &=- 2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=- \pi$.
